title: operator-decision-support-ui-prototype-and-integration-guide
author: Maya Patel
content:
## Purpose
This document defines the prototype, integration contract, and rollout plan for the Operator Decision Support UI (ODSU). The ODSU is a lightweight, read-write operator surface that consolidates prioritized telemetry, recommended playbook actions, and one-click/one-approval remediation for platform operators during inference service incidents. The goal is to reduce mean time to mitigation (MTTM) for common platform incidents by 35% while preserving safety and auditability.

## Scope and non-goals
- In scope: front-end prototype for oncall/operator workflows, backend API contracts to call authoritative runbook & orchestration services, telemetry selection & aggregation rules, basic RBAC hooks, and fallbacks for the UI when control plane is degraded.
- Out of scope: full replacement of Platform Console; deep-change automated remediation (we will limit initial actions to low-risk controls like traffic re-routes, model variant swaps, and runbook-triggered canaries).

## Goals and success metrics
- Reduce operator decision time for top-5 incident classes by 35% (measure via simulated gamedays).
- No silent automations: every action must produce a signed audit event and operator confirmation except pre-approved emergency aborts.
- SLOs for ODSU control API: 99.9% availability, median 50ms read latency for single-tenant dashboards.

## High-level UX components
1. Alert Triage Pane — prioritized alerts + short causal hints (e.g., "KV-prefix-cache miss surge + shard 42 eviction")
2. Action Suggestion Panel — deterministic recommendations with confidence level and rationale (telemetry links + relevant playbook sections)
3. Quick Actions — safe, parameterized controls (traffic-steer, model-swap, burst-credit-grant, prefix-cache-drain)
4. Runbook Launcher — opens targeted runbook sections with prefilled context from telemetry and recent traces
5. Audit & Rollback Drawer — shows all actions in the session with one-click rollback and the ability to attach notes

## Operator workflows (numbered)
1. Incident intake (token surge):
   1) Operator opens Alert Triage Pane.
   2) ODSU auto-populates tenant, model, region, recent token-rate chart, and cost-slope.
   3) Action Suggestion: "Apply soft throttle (10%) to tenant X and swap model->quantized variant" with estimated latency and cost delta.
   4) Operator clicks Quick Action -> confirmation modal -> click Approve.
   5) Control API returns success; ODSU writes audit event and annotates relevant dashboards.
2. Model fallback misfire:
   1) Triage shows spike in model-diff errors and degraded-quality alert.
   2) Suggestion: "Rollback last model rollout for route /chat/summarize".
   3) Operator triggers Runbook Launcher to validate canary traces; if checks pass operator runs rollback via ODSU (requires 2nd approver for production).

## Backend integration contract (API spec excerpts)
- Base service: platform-ops-ui-controlplane (internal service name: platform-ops-ui).
- Read endpoints (GET):
  - GET /v1/alerts?tenant={tenant}&region={region}&limit=50 -> returns list of enriched alerts.
  - GET /v1/telemetry/context?trace_id={id} -> returns pre-aggregated timeseries & top spans.
- Action endpoints (POST): all action endpoints require operator_id and request_id headers and respond with an operation id for audit.
  - POST /v1/actions/traffic-steer
  - POST /v1/actions/model-swap
  - POST /v1/actions/runbook-trigger
  - POST /v1/actions/grant-burst-credit

Example action payload (JSON):
{
  "action": "model-swap",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-8421",
  "route": "/chat/summarize",
  "from_model": "redwood-llama-v1.1",
  "to_model": "redwood-llama-v1.1-quant8",
  "operator_notes": "reduce CPU during surge; approved by lead",
  "dry_run": false
}

Transitive guarantees: backend must validate action against Policy Service (OPA) and return 403 if not permitted. All successful actions produce an audit event to audit-log-sink and a telemetry event to operator-telemetry-fanout.

## Telemetry selection and UX prioritization rules
- Signals to surface (ranked):
  1) SLO burn rate (token-latency SLO, error-rate SLO) — 15s window
  2) Token ingestion rate (per-tenant, per-route) — 10s window
  3) Recent model error diff and perplexity delta — 30s window
  4) KV prefix cache miss rate + eviction count — 60s window
  5) Cost slope (tokens/sec * cost-per-token) — 30s window
- Prioritization heuristic: score = 0.4*SLO_burn + 0.25*rate_surge + 0.15*error_diff + 0.2*cost_slope. Thresholds: score > 0.7 -> urgent; 0.4-0.7 -> investigate; <0.4 -> informational.

## SLOs and thresholds for UI availability
- Controlplane read (dashboards): 99.9% p95 latency < 200ms.
- Controlplane actions: 99.5% success within 2s (post-policy and preflight checks).
- Telemetry staleness: fall back to degraded-mode UI when telemetry lag > 90s (show last-known and warn).

## Safety & authorization
- Every state-changing action must be evaluated by OPA policy: action + tenant + route + operator_role.
- High-risk actions (model rollback, tenant eviction) require 2-person approval by default; configuration controlled via RBAC rules.
- Rate-limit operator actions at platform-ops-ui: 10 actions/operator/minute to avoid automation loops.

## Data model and required fields for action requests (table)
| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| operator_id | string | yes | canonical operator identity (SCIM id) |
| request_id | string | yes | idempotency token |
| tenant_id | string | yes | target tenant |
| route | string | conditional | recommended for route-scoped actions |
| action | string | yes | one of {traffic-steer, model-swap, runbook-trigger, grant-burst-credit} |
| params | json-string | conditional | action-specific parameters |
| dry_run | boolean | no | preview-only mode |

## Implementation plan and milestone checklist
1. Prototype (Q4 2025): static front-end + fake backend; run two gamedays with SRE + oncall.
2. Backend minimal (Q1 2026): implement read endpoints & runbook-trigger; wire audit-log-sink.
3. Policy integration (Q2 2026): OPA policy checks and RBAC hooks.
4. Quick actions (Q2 2026): allow traffic-steer and model-swap with 2-approver enforcement.
5. Operator rollout (Q3 2026): gradual rollout behind feature flag to platform-operators group; monitor MTTM and false-positive actions.

## Testing and validation checklist
- Unit + integration tests for all action endpoints; mock Policy Service for negative tests.
- Simulated Gameday scenarios for top-5 incident classes (measure operator decision time and correctness).
- Security review: ensure audit events include pre/post state and operator notes.
- Load test: 500 concurrent operators reading dashboards; 50 concurrent action requests.

## Rollout and rollback plan
- Feature-flagged rollout in three waves: internal alpha (SRE + devs) -> platform operators -> limited customer-impact subset.
- Monitoring KPIs: number of actions per operator, action success rate, action rollback rate, operator satisfaction survey.
- Rollback: revoke controlplane write traffic via feature flag; actions revert to manual CLI with full audit.

## Security & compliance notes
- All controlplane API calls must be TLS 1.2+ and require mTLS when originating from operator consoles outside GCP.
- Audit logs retained 13 months in audit-log-sink; high-risk action snapshots stored for 5 years for compliance.
- Any cross-tenant action must be reviewed with Security for PII surface (labelled restricted if PII touch predicted).

## Open questions and decisions to make
- Q1: Do we allow automated rollbacks without second approver for low-risk model rollback? (propose: no)
- Q2: What confidence threshold triggers an ODSU suggestion vs. on-demand insights? (propose: 0.6 score)
- Q3: How to represent cost tradeoffs in UI without biasing operator decisions? (propose: show estimated delta and a cost impact badge)

## Appendix: CLI examples and preflight commands
- Trigger runbook via API (requires operator token):
curl -X POST https://platform-ops-internal.redwood/v1/actions/runbook-trigger \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"runbook_id":"rb-llm-prefix-cache-eviction","context":{"tenant":"tenant-8421","shard":42}}'

- Dry-run model swap:
curl -X POST https://platform-ops-internal.redwood/v1/actions/model-swap \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"operator_id":"u-0023","request_id":"req-20260118-01","tenant_id":"tenant-8421","route":"/chat/summarize","from_model":"redwood-llama-v1.1","to_model":"redwood-llama-v1.1-quant8","dry_run":true}'
